blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Latent world models plan in a compact latent space by predicting the outcomes of actions. Their planners judge a plan by the latent distance between its
  predicted end state and the goal image. We show that this distance fails in two distinct ways. First, it loses directional signal a few steps from the
  goal, causing distant goals to fail. Second, it weighs the robot arm over the manipulated object, causing manipulation to fail at contact. We measure
  both failures directly on recorded data by asking whether a lower latent distance corresponds to true progress toward the goal. Across five
  environments, six visual representations (including raw pixels and V-JEPA 2), and nine Meta-World tasks, this ranking test cleanly separates the two
  failures, and the graph distance to a goal predicts where closed-loop planning breaks down. Both failures share a single remedy: replacing the distant
  goal with a nearby target that lies on a recorded trajectory. We realize this principle with Graph Anchors, a training-free planner for frozen latent
  world models. It builds a sparse graph once over the model's own training frames and aims each planning step at a node a few moves ahead along the
  shortest path to the goal, keeping paths on recorded transitions wherever contact matters. On goals up to 400 steps away, Graph Anchors raise LeWM's
  success from 13% to 85% on PointMaze-Medium, from 8% to 87% on PointMaze-Large, and from 5% to 71% on Push-T, where stronger search toward the goal
  fails and where prior training-free planners break down under missing step horizons, subsampling shortcuts, or fragmented contact.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: World models predict how actions change the world, allowing an agent to evaluate candidate plans in imagination before acting [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 ] . Recent visual world models predict in the latent space of an image encoder [ 31 , 38 , 25 ] and plan by sampling action sequences, rolling out their predicted futures, and keeping the actions whose final latent state lies closest to a goal image [ 7 , 35 ] . This approach works reliably for nearby goals. On PointMaze-Medium, LeWorldModel (LeWM) [ 25 ] solves 50% of goals 50 steps away, yet drops to just 13% at 200 steps, as illustrated in Figure 1 . On Push-T it solves only 5% at 150 steps, often parking the pusher while leaving the T-block behind.
blocks.zh: 世界模型预测行动如何改变世界,允许代理人在行动前用想象力评价候选计划[14,15,16,17]. 最近的视觉世界模型在图像编码器的潜在空间中预测[31,38,25],并通过取样动作序列进行计划,推出其预测的未来,并保持其最终潜在状态最接近目标图像的行动[7,35]. 这种办法对附近的目标是可靠的。 在PointMaze-Medium上,LeWorldModel(LeWM)[25]解决了50%的目标50个出站点,然而在200个出站点上却下降到只有13%,如图1所示. 在Push-T上,它在150个台阶下只解决了5%的问题,经常会把推手停放而将T-被挡后.

(b) Graph Anchors aim each plan at a nearby node (orange) along the shortest route through the recorded data (light blue), and the exact same frozen planner reaches the goal.

blocks.en: Why does a planner that easily solves short-range goals break down here? Rather than guessing, we test the latent goal cost directly. On recorded data, before running any planner, we measure how often a lower latent distance corresponds to a move that genuinely progresses toward the goal ( Section 4.1 ). This simple test isolates two root failures. The first is range : latent distance ranks local moves accurately right next to the goal, but loses directional signal within a few graph hops across every navigation task and across six visual encoders, including raw pixels, DINOv2, CLIP, SigLIP, V-JEPA 2, and LeWM ( Section A.1 ). The second is focus : whole-image distance weighs the robot arm far more heavily than the manipulated object, preferring an accurate arm pose over completing the task across all nine Meta-World [ 42 ] object tasks we measure ( Section A.2 ).
blocks.zh: 为什么一个容易解决短距离入球的计划员会在这里破裂? 而不是猜测, 我们测试潜在的目标 成本直接。 根据记录的数据,在运行任何规划员之前,我们衡量低潜距在多大程度上与真正朝向目标迈进的动作相对应(第4.1节)。 这个简单的测试隔离出两个根故障. 第一个是范围:潜在距离将局部移动精确地排到目标旁边,但在每个导航任务和6个视觉编码器,包括原始像素、DINOv2、CLIP、SigLIP、V-JEPA 2和LEWM(A.1节)的几个图跳中失去方向信号。 第二是焦点:全相距比被操纵的物体重得多地重于机器人手臂,更倾向于精确的手臂,而不是完成我们测量的所有9个Meta-World[42]物体任务(A.2节).

blocks.en: Importantly, both failures have the exact same remedy. Whole-image distance works reliably whenever its target is nearby and lies along a route recorded in the data. On Meta-World, keeping the released cost untouched and simply aiming at a demonstration frame 20 steps ahead solves 65 of 72 object episodes that the final goal image never solves. We introduce Graph Anchors to provide such targets automatically without demonstrations or retraining. We construct a sparse graph once over the world model’s own training frames, compute a shortest path to the goal, and aim each planning step at an anchor node a few moves ahead on that path. Where object contact matters, penalizing cross-episode jumps keeps the route on continuous recorded transitions. With the released search and world model untouched, replacing only the distant goal with our nearby anchor lifts PointMaze-Medium at 200 steps from 12% to 85%, whereas stronger search aimed at the distant goal stalls at 9%. On Push-T, preserving recorded transitions raises d = 150 d{=}150 success from 30% to 71%.
blocks.zh: 重要的是,两种失败都有同样的补救办法。 只要目标在附近,而且位于数据记录的路线沿线,全图像距离就可靠地工作。 在"Meta-World"上,保持所释放出的成本不受影响,并简单地瞄准一个演示框架,提前20步解决了最终目标图像从未解决的72个对象中65个. 我们引入了图指针,以自动提供此类目标,而不进行演示或再培训。 我们曾经在世界模型的训练框架上绘制出一幅稀有的图,计算出最短的通向目标的道路,并且把每个规划步骤都放在一个锚点上,沿着这条道路向前走几步。 在对象接触事项上,对跨集跳跃的处罚使路由保持在连续被记录的过渡上. 仅用我们附近的主播取代遥远的入球, 将点马兹-中子从12%升至85%, 在 Push-T 上,保存有记录的转换将 D = 150 d = 150 成功率从 30%提高到 71%.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are threefold: • A direct diagnosis of the latent goal cost. A local ranking test on recorded data separates two distinct failures, range and focus , across five environments, six image representations, and nine Meta-World tasks. Offline graph distance predicts where closed-loop planning fails, and a formal drift analysis ( Section A.3 ) connects local ranking to linear versus quadratic reaching times. • Graph Anchors. A simple, training-free planner for frozen latent world models that cures both failures using nearby anchors on recorded routes, changing only the target and scoring rule of the planner while leaving the encoder, predictor, and CEM optimizer untouched. • Long-horizon evaluation and failure analysis of alternative planners. Across goals up to 400 steps away on navigation and manipulation, we benchmark against world-model planners, offline goal-conditioned policies, graph-guided policies (GAS [ 4 ] , TTGS [ 30 ] ), and training-free world-model planners (AP [ 23 ] , NGC [ 41 ] , Metro-WM [ 20 ] ), showing how each missing diagnostic axis causes specific structural failures ( Section 5.5 , Appendix D ).
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献有三:直接诊断潜在的目标成本。 本地对记录数据的排名测试将两个不同的失败, 范围和焦点, 跨越了五个环境, 六个图像表达, 九个Meta-World任务。 离线图相距预测闭路规划失败的地方,正式的漂移分析(A.3节)将本地排名与线性对四相到达时间相接. • 地图锁定器。 一个简单的,无训练的 冷冻潜在世界模型计划者 利用附近的锚在记录的路线上 治愈两种故障, 仅仅改变目标 和计程者评分规则 同时离开编码器, 预测器, 和CEM 优化器。 • 对替代规划者进行长期评价和失败分析。 在航行和操纵方面,我们在400多步之外的目标中,参照世界模型规划者、附带目标条件的离线政策、图表指导政策(GAS[4]、TTGS[30])和无培训的世界模型规划者(AP[23]、NGC[41]、Metro-WM[20]),说明每个缺失的诊断轴如何造成具体的结构故障(第5.5节,附录D)。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: World models predict the consequences of actions in a learned latent space [ 14 , 15 , 16 ] and support planning via model-predictive control [ 7 , 17 ] . For visual goal reaching, DINO-WM [ 45 ] plans with CEM over predicted DINOv2 [ 31 ] patch features, PLDM [ 38 ] learns latent dynamics from reward-free offline trajectories, and LeWM [ 25 ] trains encoder and predictor jointly from pixels with a joint-embedding objective [ 2 ] . JEPA-WM [ 40 ] studies the design choices behind such planners, and V-JEPA 2 [ 3 ] extends them to robot actions. These planners minimize latent distance to a goal image and are typically evaluated around 25 steps ahead. Recent work improves the predictor [ 8 , 13 ] or questions the goal cost directly: Temporal-Distance JEPA [ 5 ] and TEMPO [ 28 ] learn temporal distances, Li et al. [ 21 ] learn reachability metrics, Singh [ 37 ] shows that LeWM’s latent distance misrepresents progress on Two-Room, and Alrasheed et al. [ 1 ] find that world models rank actions reliably only near their imagined horizon. We measure directional ranking directly against graph distance and against scene elements, and keep the world model and cost completely unchanged.
blocks.zh: 世界模型预测在已学到的潜在空间中采取行动的后果[14、15、16],并通过模型预测控制支持规划[7、17]。 为达到可视目标,DINO-WM[45]计划与CEM相比预测的DINOv2[31]补丁特性,PLDM[38]从无酬离线轨迹中学习出潜伏的动力学,而LeWM[25]列车编码器和预测器则联合从有联合嵌入目标的像素中学习出[2]. JEPA-WM [40] 研究这些规划者背后的设计选择,而V-JEPA 2 [3] 将其扩展至机器人动作. 这些规划者尽可能地减少与目标图像的潜在距离,通常在25个步骤之前进行评估。 最近的工作改进了预测器[8,13]或直接质疑目标成本:Timoral-Distance JEPA [5]和TEMPO [28]学习时间距离,李等. [21] 学习可达性衡量标准, Singh [37] 显示LEWM的潜在距离歪曲了"双室"上的进展,以及Alrasheed等人. [1]发现,世界模型对动作的排序可靠,只接近其想象的地平线. 我们直接对照图表距离和场景元素测量方向排名,保持世界模型和成本完全不变.

blocks.en: Earlier visual planners reached goal images with pixel-space models [ 11 ] or planned over intermediate subgoals proposed by learned generative models [ 29 , 34 ] . HWM [ 44 ] trains world models at multiple temporal scales, FF-JEPA [ 26 ] predicts intermediate subgoals, SAGE [ 6 ] trains a subgoal generator and action proposal model for LeWM, and PILOT [ 24 ] generates visual subgoals with a video model. All of these require training new components. Graph Anchors instead retrieve subgoals directly from the world model’s existing training data, requiring no additional training whenever the data covers the route.
blocks.zh: 早期的视觉规划者用像素-空间模型[11]或规划在已学到的基因模型[29,34]提出的中间次级目标上实现了目标图像. HWM[44]在多时尺度上训练出世界模型,FF-JEPA[26]预测中间次级目标,SAGE[6]为LEWM训练出一个次级目标生成器和行动建议模型,而PLOT[24]用视频模型生成视觉次级目标. 所有这些都需要培训新的组成部分。 反之,图定点直接取自世界模式现有培训数据中的次级目标,只要数据涵盖该路线,就不需要额外培训。

blocks.en: SPTM [ 36 ] links observations by temporal adjacency and learned reachability, SoRB [ 10 ] plans over stored states with a goal-conditioned value function, HTM [ 22 ] and L3P [ 43 ] search graphs of generated images and learned landmarks, and sparse graphical memory [ 9 ] and landmark graphs [ 18 ] maintain compact state graphs for goal reaching. More recently, GAS [ 4 ] builds a graph in a learned temporal-distance space for a low-level policy, and TTGS [ 30 ] searches an offline dataset over learned value distances to guide a frozen policy. Three other training-free planners retarget a frozen LeWM directly: Anchored Planning (AP) [ 23 ] retrieves the single-episode segment best matching the current frame and goal given the step count d d , NGC [ 41 ] replaces latent distance with shortest-path length over a subsampled undirected graph, and Metro-WM [ 20 ] retrieves subgoals from a sparse graph of recorded frames. We compare all six paradigms directly under our diagnostic framework in Section 5.5 and Appendix D .

Following LeWM [ 25 ] , each action is a block of five consecutive environment steps. At test time, the agent observes o 1 o_{1} and receives a goal image o g o_{g} , succeeding if it reaches the goal within its step budget.

blocks.en: 4 Graph Anchors
blocks.zh: 4 相图锁定

blocks.en: We first diagnose why latent planning breaks down at long range and during object contact ( Section 4.1 ). We then present three lightweight components that address both failures without modifying or retraining the world model ( Figure 3 ): a sparse graph of recorded frames supplying nearby anchors on a shortest path ( Sections 4.2 and 4.3 ), an episode-switch cost that keeps routes on continuous recorded transitions ( Section 4.4 ), and closest-approach scoring that guides rollouts smoothly through each anchor ( Section 4.5 ).
blocks.zh: 我们首先分析潜在规划为何在远距离和物体接触期间破裂(第4.1节)。 然后,我们提出三个轻量级组件,在不修改或再培训世界模式的情况下处理两种故障(图3):在最短的路由上提供附近锚的被记录框架的稀有图表(第4.2和4.3节),使航道保持连续被记录的过渡(第4.4节)的分数,以及指导顺利通过每个锚地展开的最接近的分数(第4.5节)。

blocks.en: The planner of Section 3 fails in these settings for three coupled reasons.
blocks.zh: 第三节的规划者在这些设置中失败,原因有三个。

blocks.en: First, whole-image distance has a short range . Across every navigation benchmark, ρ ⁡ ( h ) \rho(h) starts near 1 right next to the goal and drops to 0.50–0.59 within six hops ( Figure 2 a). Section A.1 verifies the exact same collapse directly along recorded time steps without building any graph. Measuring hops on a true-position reference graph, LeWM, PLDM, and frozen DINOv2 all start at 0.93–0.98 and fall below 0.55 within 6–9 hops on PointMaze-Medium ( Figure 2 b). In Section A.1 we further test raw pixels, CLIP, SigLIP, and video-trained V-JEPA 2 alongside 10-epoch training checkpoints ( Figures A2 and A2 ). Because even raw pixels decay at the exact same rate as V-JEPA 2, short range is an inherent property of comparing two whole images across corridors and walls rather than an undertrained encoder. Far from the goal, heavier search cannot rescue the planner because candidate rollouts are ranked by a directionless score: doubling the horizon leaves Example 1 at 12%. Section 4.3 cures this by replacing the distant goal with a nearby target.

blocks.en: Second, whole-image distance has the wrong focus . In Example 2, overall ρ \rho decays slowly, so range alone does not explain why Push-T fails. Because whole-image distance averages over all pixels, a large robot arm or agent dominates a small manipulated object. Testing the released JEPA-WM planner [ 40 ] on Meta-World [ 42 ] by placing arm and object independently with inverse kinematics shows that shifting only the hand by 5 cm costs 2.6 to 14 × \times more than leaving only the object off target across all nine object tasks ( Figure 2 c), a bias that persists across raw pixels, DINOv2, CLIP, SigLIP, and V-JEPA 2 ( Figure A6 ), even though a linear probe on the exact same frozen features locates the object cleanly ( Section A.2 ). Under exact simulator dynamics, the released cost solves 0 of 72 object episodes. Merely picking a closer target is not enough either: on Push-T, an anchor three hops ahead without preserving recorded transitions stays at 30%. However, aiming the unchanged released cost at a nearby frame on a recorded route , such as the frame 20 steps ahead on the episode’s own demonstration, immediately solves 65 of 72 Meta-World episodes ( Figure 2 d). Matching a nearby recorded arm pose naturally moves the object as recorded. Section 4.4 preserves recorded transitions automatically inside our graph.

blocks.en: Why does chaining local latent neighbours cure long-range failure? Frames that are close in latent space are physically close in the environment: on PointMaze-Medium and Two-Room, virtually none (0%) of a frame’s ten nearest latent neighbours sits more than one maze cell away by walking distance ( Figure 4 a), and checking all 994,834 unique neighbour edges on PointMaze-Medium yields zero wall crossings ( Section B.2 ). Over long distances, direct latent distance breaks down: rank correlation with true walking distance on PointMaze-Medium drops from 0.97 near the goal to 0.17 far from it ( Figure 4 b). Shortest-path hops over the local neighbour graph hold correlation at 0.69 far from the goal, and raise Two-Room from 0.05 to 0.50. The graph therefore handles global routing while the visual cost only needs to rank the last few hops to a nearby anchor.

In contact manipulation (Example 2), a nearby anchor alone is insufficient. On Push-T, unweighted shortest paths follow a recorded temporal transition on only 45% of hops, and only 29% carry recorded block motion; typical cross-episode jumps shift the T-block by 22 px with no recorded push connecting them. To keep paths on continuous recorded pushes, we charge a higher edge weight λ ≥ 1 \lambda\geq 1 on cross-episode neighbour edges: w ⁡ ( i , j ) = { 1 , ( i , j ) ∈ E T , λ , ( i , j ) ∈ E N ∖ E T , w(i,j)=\begin{cases}1,&(i,j)\in E_{T},\\

blocks.en: Graph Anchors also transfer to other world models whenever their local dynamics are accurate: on Two-Room, adding anchors lifts PLDM from 50% to 97% and DINO-WM (over frozen DINOv2 latents) from 70% to 95%, whereas on PointMaze-Medium PLDM (4%) and DINO-WM (20%) cannot reliably reach targets six hops away. blocks.en: Push-T exposes focus failure most sharply, and the contact setting ( K = 2 , λ = 3 K{=}2,\lambda{=}3 ) makes a dramatic difference: at d = 150 d{=}150 it reaches 71%, compared to 30% for the navigation setting and 65% for AP [ 23 ] on identical pairs ( Figure 7 c). On Cube, gains are more modest (26% to 39%, remaining below AP’s 53%) because 15 of 40 navigation failures never initiate contact with the cube; a recorded trajectory alone cannot synthesize a delicate grasp. On medium mazes, the contact setting remains strong at 94% on PointMaze-Medium and 100% on Two-Room, trading off slight efficiency on stitched routes (91% versus 95%) and short-range Reacher (54% versus 68%).

blocks.en: Ablating our three components one by one confirms their distinct roles ( Figure 7 ). On PointMaze-Medium, changing the target alone accounts for nearly the entire gain ( Figure 7 a): aiming LeWM’s unchanged search at our anchors lifts success from 12% to 85%, while aiming our closest-approach search at the distant goal stays at 9%. Heavier search toward the goal cannot replace anchors either: doubling the horizon and more than tripling CEM samples leaves goal-aimed planning at 28% on PointMaze-Medium and 77% on Two-Room, far below default anchors in the same runs (89% and 94%, Table A9 b). On Two-Room, both target and closest-approach search contribute (66% to 94%). Finally, on Push-T, the switch cost λ = 3 \lambda{=}3 is the decisive contact ingredient: shrinking the anchor to K = 3 K{=}3 without λ = 3 \lambda{=}3 stays at 30%, whereas adding λ = 3 \lambda{=}3 jumps immediately to 72% ( Figure 7 c).

blocks.en: 5.4 Which Design Choices Matter?

blocks.en: Anchor span K K balances directional signal against progress per decision ( Figure 7 b). Placing anchors too far ( K = 12 K{=}12 ) reintroduces range failure, dropping PointMaze-Medium from 83% at K = 6 K{=}6 to 35%, whereas K = 2 K{=}2 stalls under fixed 5-block navigation execution at 57% (resolved by short-horizon closest-approach execution in Table A10 b). Optimal span increases with horizon H H , from K = 4 K{=}4 at H = 5 H{=}5 to K = 6 K{=}6 at H = 10 H{=}10 , with K = 6 K{=}6 staying within 6 points of optimal across the entire grid ( Table A10 a). Cross-episode neighbour edges are indispensable: removing them collapses PointMaze-Medium from 86% to 6%, while varying k ∈ { 5 , 10 , 20 } k\in\{5,10,20\} barely changes results ( Figure A13 b).

blocks.en: Graph Anchors are also remarkably robust to scarce or shifted data ( Figure 9 and Table A11 ). On PointMaze-Medium d = 200 d{=}200 , keeping just 1% of training episodes still reaches 63%, and building the graph purely from random play reaches 90%. On PointMaze-Large d = 400 d{=}400 , indexing a separate unseen dataset never used during world-model training still achieves 87%. Finally, mid-episode displacement (kidnapping) requires no special recovery logic: replanning re-anchors from the new observation automatically, shifting success only from 86% to 65%.

blocks.en: 5.5 Diagnosing Training-Free World-Model Planners (AP, NGC, Metro-WM)
blocks.zh: 5.5 诊断无培训的世界模式规划者(AP、NGC、Metro-WM)

blocks.en: Our diagnosis identifies four practical requirements for training-free long-horizon visual planning: (i) a reliable short-range controller, (ii) a sparse graph scaling to 100% of frames without subsampling shortcuts, (iii) preserved recorded transitions where contact matters, and (iv) target-search decoupling without oracle step counts or fragile per-task horizon coupling. Table 2 maps prior graph-guided policies (GAS [ 4 ] , TTGS [ 30 ] ) and training-free world-model planners (AP [ 23 ] , NGC [ 41 ] , Metro-WM [ 20 ] ) onto these exact axes. We re-implemented AP, NGC, and Metro-WM inside our shared evaluation framework on identical frozen checkpoints, 5-step training nodes, seeds, and 2 ​ d 2d budgets; Table A16 verifies that all three match their published results within 9 points despite our tighter 2 ​ d 2d budget.

blocks.en: Staying inside one recorded episode preserves contact continuity, explaining AP’s strong Push-T and Cube scores when given the exact step distance d d . However, omitting a graph forces AP to know d d in advance and limits it to routes covered by a single training episode. When d d is off by 2 2 – 3 × 3\times ( Figure 10 d, Table A17 c), the eligible episode bank shrinks drastically and 21–78% of retrieved starts fall across solid maze walls, dropping PointMaze-Medium from 80% to 11%, Two-Room from 97% to 2%, and Push-T from 65% to 16% ( 0.5 × 0.5\times ) and 0% ( 3 × 3\times ). AP breaks similarly whenever single episodes cannot span the task: stitched goals (23.3% across-wall starts, Figure 11 d), PointMaze-Large (18% and 9% versus our 76% and 45%), mid-episode kidnapping (22% vs. 65%), random-play data (56% vs. 94%), and Reacher (34% vs. 68%).

blocks.en: Replacing Euclidean distance with shortest-path length over 5,000 undirected snapshots solves medium mazes (100% on PointMaze-Medium), but violates two axes. First, discarding directed temporal edges creates a clear geometry-vs.-executability gap on Push-T ( Figure 10 b, Table A17 a): NGC scores higher offline object-pose ranking accuracy ( ρ obj = 0.715 \rho_{\text{obj}}{=}0.715 ) than Graph Anchors (0.649) because undirected snapshots hop across state space without obeying pushing physics, yet 65.9% of its route hops teleport the block over 15 px (up to 217 px / 131 ∘ in Figure 11 e), collapsing closed-loop Push-T to 11% at d = 150 d{=}150 and 4% at d = 200 d{=}200 . Second, storing an N × N N{\times}N distance table and re-attaching every CEM candidate hits an O ⁡ ( N 2 ) O(N^{2}) wall ( Figure 10 c): on an RTX 3090 Ti, N = 5,000 N{=}5{,}000 already takes 95.4 MB and 1,729.9 ms per decision, while full datasets would require 148 GB on PointMaze-Medium and 789 GB on Push-T. Capping N = 5,000 N{=}5{,}000 on 200k-frame PointMaze-Large forces 9.51% of edges into false long-jump shortcuts up to 22.8 maze units, collapsing NGC to 24% / 20%. Graph Anchors indexes all 199k–200k nodes in 72.9 MB and 64.6 ms per decision, running 26.8 × 26.8\times faster.

blocks.en: Metro-WM builds a sparse frame graph like ours, directly isolating why our three design choices matter. First, checking 80,000 Push-T bridges shows that 87.6% are priced below a real 5-frame temporal edge (median 1.32 frames; 100% on PointMaze-Large). Dijkstra therefore abandons recorded pushes immediately ( Figure 10 b, Figure 11 f), splitting Push-T into 7.03 switches per 6 moves and stalling success at 33% ( d = 150 d{=}150 ) and 27% ( d = 200 d{=}200 ). Our switch cost λ = 3 \lambda{=}3 cuts switches 4.2 × 4.2\times to 1.68, stretches unbroken pushes 2.7 × 2.7\times to 5.40 moves ( Figure 11 g), and lifts Push-T d = 150 d{=}150 to 71%. Second, scaling bridge radius with budget H H admits sparse-data shortcuts: on 1% PointMaze-Medium data ( Figure 11 b), 1.88% of bridges exceed a real 5-step move up to 3.0 × 3.0\times (dropping success from 98% to 76–78%), versus 0.00% shortcuts for our fixed 1-block τ \tau . Third, executing fixed- h h terminal-cost plans prevents any ( h , H ) (h,H) pair from transferring across tasks ( Figure 10 d): Two-Room’s best ( 1 : 10 1{:}10 , 100%) drops to 8% on Push-T d = 150 d{=}150 , while PointMaze-Medium’s best ( 3 : 20 3{:}20 , 98%) drops to 72% on Two-Room, 33% on Push-T, and 6% on PointMaze-Large d = 400 d{=}400 . Full reproduction checks, Push-T distance curves through d = 200 d{=}200 , and complete numbers appear in Section D.2 .

blocks.en: Our diagnosis also predicts where Graph Anchors help before running any evaluation. First, aiming at a nearby target restores positive closed-loop drift. Counting progress in hops on a true-state reference graph, fewer than half of LeWM’s decisions end closer to the goal on all three traced benchmarks. Adding Graph Anchors raises improving decisions to 72% on PointMaze-Medium, 74% on Two-Room, and 53% on Push-T ( Table 4 and Section A.3 ). As Proposition 1 proves, positive net drift changes expected hitting time from quadratic Ω ⁡ ( D 2 ) \Omega(D^{2}) random wandering to linear O ⁡ ( D ) O(D) progress.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: The visual goal cost of a latent world model ranks local progress accurately only when its target is nearby and lies on a recorded route. Measuring this directly separates two root failures, range and focus , explains why distant goals and contact tasks collapse, and predicts where retrieved subgoals help. Graph Anchors put this finding to work without modifying or retraining the world model, using a sparse full-dataset graph, cross-episode switch penalties, and closest-approach scoring to remove range failure across mazes and focus failure on Push-T while avoiding the step-horizon fragility, quadratic scaling wall, and contact fragmentation of alternative training-free planners.
blocks.zh: 潜在世界模型的可视目标成本,只有当其目标接近并且位于有记录的路线上时,才精确地将当地的进展排序为一等. 衡量这一点直接将两个根本失败(范围与重点)区分开来,解释为什么遥远的目标和联系任务会崩溃,并预测检索的次级目标能帮助哪些地方。 Graph Anchors将这个发现放在工作上,而没有修改或再培训世界模型,使用一个稀少的全数据集图,跨集开关惩罚,以及最接近的取号来去除整个迷宫的射程故障并聚焦于Push-T上的故障,同时避免了步距脆弱,四相缩放墙,以及其他无培训规划者的接触破碎.

blocks.en: Graph Anchors rely on recorded trajectories covering the route and use two task-level settings for navigation versus contact; the contact setting trades off efficiency on long stitched mazes and short-range Reacher. Because a recorded route cannot synthesize a delicate grasp when the local world model misses initial contact, Cube remains below AP, and our Meta-World demonstration test serves as an exact-dynamics upper bound rather than a deployable manipulation controller. Extending training-free graph guidance to dexterous grasping and open-world video world models remains an exciting direction for future work.
blocks.zh: Graph Anchors 依赖于覆盖路线的已记录的轨迹,并使用两个任务级别设置进行导航与接触;这种接触在长缝迷宫和短程雷彻上对效率进行交易。 由于一个被记录的路径无法在本地世界模型错过初始接触时合成出微妙的抓取,Cube仍然低于AP,而我们的Meta-World演示测试充当了精确的动力学上方约束而不是可部署的操纵控制器. 将无培训图示指导扩展至能灵活把握和开放世界的视频世界模式,仍然是未来工作的令人振奋的方向.

blocks.en: On the standard 25-step LeWM evaluation setup summarized in Table A1 , both visual world-model planners and offline policies solve most goals easily. Once the goal is placed further away, however, those same planners break down sharply. As shown in Figure 6 and Table A6 , LeWM drops to 13% at d = 200 d{=}200 on PointMaze-Medium, 31% at d = 75 d{=}75 on Two-Room, 5% at d = 150 d{=}150 on Push-T, and 8% at d = 400 d{=}400 on PointMaze-Large.
blocks.zh: 在表A1概述的标准25步LEWM评价设置上,视觉世界模型规划者和离线政策都轻松地解决了大多数目标. 然而,一旦将目标放在更远的地方,这些规划者就会急剧崩溃。 如图6和表A6所示,LEWM在Point Maze-Medium上下降至13%,在d=200 d{=}200,在d=75 d{=}75,在Push-T上下降5%,在d=400 d{=}400。

blocks.en: Simply throwing more search compute at the distant goal does not rescue the planner. Doubling the planning horizon and more than tripling the number of CEM samples lifts LeWM to only 28% on PointMaze-Medium and 77% on Two-Room in Table A9 b. Even switching to our closest-approach scoring while still aiming at the distant goal stays at 9% on PointMaze-Medium in Table A9 a. Tracing closed-loop rollouts in true-state graph hops reveals what goes wrong at runtime. Fewer than half of LeWM’s decisions actually end closer to the goal, with only 48% improving on PointMaze-Medium, 33% on Two-Room, and 31% on Push-T, as documented in Table 4 and Table A4 .
blocks.zh: 仅仅在遥远的球门上投出更多的搜索计算 并不能拯救计划者 将计划范围翻一番,将CEM样本数量翻了三倍以上,使LEWM在PointMaze-Medium上升至28%,在表A9b中为2-Room上升至77%。 即使切换到我们最接近的分数,同时仍然瞄准远方目标,仍然保持在表A9 a中的PointMaze-Medium上的9%. 追踪在真实状态图跳出闭路 显示运行时出错 正如表4和表A4所记录的,不到一半的LEWM决定实际上接近目标,在PointMaze-Medium上只有48%的改善,在双室上只有33%,在Push-T上只有31%。

blocks.zh: A.1 跨编码器和编码器的区域故障

blocks.en: To test whether a latent distance actually guides an agent toward a distant goal, we ask a simple local question. Suppose the agent is at a recorded frame v v that lies h h graph hops from a goal frame g g , and consider two neighbours u u and u ′ u^{\prime} of v v where one is genuinely closer to g g than the other. We count a latent distance as correct on this pair if it assigns a smaller cost to whichever neighbour is truly closer to g g . The ranking accuracy ρ ⁡ ( h ) \rho(h) is the share of pairs ordered correctly. A value of ρ = 1 \rho{=}1 means the distance always points downhill toward the goal, whereas ρ = 1 2 \rho{=}\tfrac{1}{2} carries no directional information and is no better than flipping a coin.

blocks.en: To avoid any circularity with a model’s own latent graph, all cross-encoder and training-epoch checks below measure hops on a fixed reference graph built strictly from ground-truth positions. This reference graph connects consecutive recorded frames along each episode and adds edges between frames closer in physical position than the median five-step move. Every encoder is tested on the exact same five-step frames drawn from a seeded fifth of the episodes, over 200 goals with up to four frames per goal and hop. Shaded bands in the plots mark 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over goals.
blocks.zh: 为了避免任何带有模型自身潜入图的循环,所有跨编码器和培训时段的检查都使用严格从地面真实位置建立的固定参考图。 此参考图沿每集连接相继被记录的帧并会比中位数的五步移动更接近物理位置的帧相间的边缘. 每个编码器都通过从第五集种子中抽取的完全相同的五步框进行测试,超过200个入球,每个入球和跳出最多有4个入球框. 在图案中被遮住的带子 标出95%的靴子置信间隔

blocks.en: The raw-pixel control highlights why this happens. Because raw pixel distance decays just like every learned encoder, including video-trained V-JEPA 2, short range is not a flaw of a specific architecture or training loss. It is a basic property of judging progress by direct distance between two whole images when walls and corridors lie between them. Figure A4 and Figure A5 show this geometry visually. Far from the goal, every encoder treats frames in distant corridors or behind solid walls as just as close to the goal as frames sitting on the true path.
blocks.zh: 生像素控制器凸显了为什么会发生这种情况. 因为原始像素相距的衰变与所学的每一个编码器一样,包括视频训练的V-JEPA 2,短距离并不是特定架构或训练损失的缺陷. 它是在墙和走廊之间用两个整体图像之间的直接距离来判断进展的基本财产。 图A4和图A5显示这种几何视觉. 与入球相去甚远,每个编码器都把远道走廊或固壁后方的相框像坐在正道上的相框一样靠近入球.

blocks.en: One might wonder whether short range simply reflects an undertrained world model. To check this, we run the exact same ranking test across every epoch from 1 to 10 of our second PointMaze-Large LeWM training run from Section C.1 , keeping raw pixels as a control. As shown in Figure A2 , extended training does not fix the decay. One hop from the goal, every checkpoint is already highly accurate, moving from 0.98 at epoch 1 to 0.99 at epoch 10. Six hops away, ρ ⁡ ( 6 ) \rho(6) shifts only from 0.55 to 0.57, staying slightly below raw pixels at 0.59. Twelve hops away, accuracy remains right at chance from 0.51 to 0.49. Over all ten epochs, the hop where ranking drops below 0.55 moves only from hop 6 to hop 8. Combined with the five-epoch PLDM check above, this confirms that longer training does not extend visual range.

blocks.en: A.2 Focus Failure Across Encoders and Pushing
blocks.zh: A.2 在整个编码器和推进中聚焦失败

blocks.en: Short range explains why planners fail on mazes, but Push-T exposes a second obstacle. On Push-T, the latent cost still ranks local moves well six hops from the goal with ρ ⁡ ( 6 ) = 0.74 \rho(6){=}0.74 , yet closed-loop planning still falls to 5% at d = 150 d{=}150 . This second failure concerns what whole-image distance actually weighs.

Figure A6: Every image distance weighs the robot arm over the object. Bars show the median exchange rate over 30 inverse-kinematics placements per task across five visual representations. This ratio divides the feature distance of shifting only the robot hand by 5 cm by the distance of leaving only the object off target by its success threshold. Shaded rows mark reach tasks where positioning the arm is the entire task. Anywhere to the right of the dashed line, the cost prefers fixing a small hand error over completing the task.

blocks.en: We next measure how strongly an image distance favors the robot arm over the object. Using inverse kinematics, we place the arm and the object independently across 30 configurations in each of eleven Meta-World tasks. We then compute the exchange rate , defined as the feature distance caused by shifting only the hand by 5 cm divided by the distance caused by leaving only the object off target by its success threshold. Any value above 1 means the visual cost prefers fixing a small hand error over finishing the task.

Both the released visual distance and TEMPO [ 28 ] , a learned temporal-distance cost that remains dominated by arm travel time, solve 0% of the six object tasks. blocks.en: Second, we leave the released cost, the CEM search, and exact dynamics completely unchanged, and replace only the final goal image with the encoded frame 20 steps ahead on the test episode’s own demonstration. That single change solves 65 of 72 object episodes, averaging 90% with 50% on push . Because this check reads from the test demonstration, it acts as a privileged upper bound rather than a deployable method. Even so, it establishes a unifying principle. Even the unchanged whole-image distance succeeds at manipulation when its target is nearby and lies on a recorded route , because matching the arm pose along a recorded trajectory automatically moves the object as recorded. Graph Anchors turns this principle into a deployable, training-free planner ( Section 4 and Appendix B ).
blocks.zh: 第二,我们让公布的费用、CEM搜索和确切动态完全不变,在测试插曲本身的演示中,只用编码框前20步替换最终目标图像。 这个单调解决了72个物体中的65个, 平均90%, 由于这个检查是从测试演示中读取的,它起到特权上限的作用,而不是一种可部署的方法. 即使如此,它确立了一项统一的原则。 即使是没有改变的全图像距离,在目标靠近并位于被记录的路线上时也会成功被操纵,因为将臂沿被记录的轨迹相匹配会自动移动被记录的对象. 图表控制器将这一原则转变为一个可部署的、无培训的规划员(第4节和附录B)。

Goal-aimed LeWM planners end only 0.42–0.51 of decisions closer to the goal, whereas Graph Anchors end 0.67–0.83 closer. • Mean drift. Immediately after a non-improving decision, Graph Anchors still drift at − - 1.3 hops while LeWM stays flat at +0.02. blocks.en: It is worth noting that Lemma 1 is a sufficient condition rather than a literal picture of every decision. In practice, an executed move often stops partway before reaching its active anchor. Measured in straight-line node steps of one median five-step move, PointMaze-Medium anchors begin 4.4 node steps away and come within 2.1 at closest approach. Across decisions, the agent reaches within 1 and 2 node steps on 21% and 49% of moves on PointMaze-Medium, 60% and 78% on Two-Room, and 24% and 55% on Push-T. Reference-graph hops make this approach look slightly smaller because fine-grained reference edges are shorter than a full recorded move. For example, on Two-Room the median closest approach is 0.7 node steps compared to 5 reference hops, and on PointMaze-Medium the agent ends closer to its anchor on 60–65% of decisions in straight-line distance versus 23–26% in reference hops. What Proposition 1 actually requires, however, is steady net drift toward the final goal, which Figure A7 a, Figure A7 b, and Table A4 verify directly.
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,Lemma 1是一个充分的条件,而不是每个决定的字面描述. 实际上,一个被执行的动作往往在到达其活动锚地之前会停止去向. 以一中位五相移动的直线节点步骤来测量,PointMaze-Medium锚地开始从4.4节点步骤向外走并最接近处进入2.1. 在所有决定中,该剂在两个节点步骤内到达了 PointMaze-Medium 的 21% 和 49% 、 二室 的 60% 和 78% 、 Push-T 的 24% 和 55% 。 参考图跳让这个方法看起来略为小一些,因为精细的参考边比完整的记录动作短。 例如,在 " 二室 " 上,最接近的中位点步骤是0.7个节点步骤,而参考跳点为5个;在 " 点马兹-中位点 " 上,该剂在60-65%的直线距离决定上接近其锚地,而参考跳点为23-26%。 然而,提议1实际上要求的是,向最终目标稳步的净漂移,图A7 a、图A7 b和表A4直接核实。

blocks.en: Graph Anchors turns the diagnosis of Section 4.1 and Appendix A into a simple planning method without changing or retraining the world model. As detailed in Algorithm A1 , the method builds a sparse latent graph once from training trajectories, selects an anchor a few moves ahead along the shortest path to the goal at each replanning step, and scores candidate CEM rollouts by their closest approach to that nearby anchor.
blocks.zh: 图表控制器将第4.1节和附录A的诊断转化为一种简单的规划方法,而不改变或再培训世界模式。 正如算法A1所详述的,该方法从训练轨迹中构建出一个稀少的潜伏图,在每个规划步骤中选择一个最短的路径前进几步,并通过最接近附近的锚来评分CEM推出的候选人。

blocks.en: We encode every fifth frame, corresponding to one action block, of every training episode with the frozen encoder and link consecutive frames by directed temporal edges as shown in Figure A8 a. To stitch routes across different trajectories, we add bidirectional neighbour edges from each node to its k = 10 k{=}10 nearest latent neighbours whose squared latent distance falls below τ \tau . As illustrated in Figure A8 b, τ \tau is set automatically to the empirical median squared latent length of a single recorded action block. Because τ \tau comes directly from the model’s own typical one-step jump size, no environment-specific distance threshold needs to be tuned. On PointMaze-Medium this builds 199k nodes, 194k temporal edges, and 2.0 M neighbour edges. Figure A8 c and Figure A8 d show that 99.9% of neighbour edges connect distinct episodes at physical separations far smaller than one five-step move. Test episodes are always removed before evaluation so no anchor can ever replay a test trajectory.

blocks.en: All evaluations use the released stable-worldmodel framework [ 25 ] with 224 × 224 224{\times}224 images, 5-step action blocks, a step budget of 2 ​ d 2d , and each environment’s native success criteria. Every random seed fixes the exact same 50 start and goal pairs and identical CEM noise across methods. Push-T, Two-Room, Cube, and Reacher use the released LeWM checkpoints and datasets, while PointMaze-Medium uses the public D4RL LeWM checkpoint of [ 19 ] verified for safe class loading. Because PointMaze-Large has no released checkpoint, we train LeWM with its default script on OGBench pointmaze-large-navigate for 10 epochs of 3,000 batches on one GPU over 1,000 episodes of 1,000 steps. As summarized in Table A5 , this yields 200 k nodes, 199 k temporal edges, and 2.3 M neighbour edges. For the unseen-dataset graph in Figure 9 , we render OGBench pointmaze-large-stitch with the exact same environment class, verify pixel and encoding agreement against stored training frames, and encode those frames with the frozen model.

Push-T,Two-Room,Cube,和Reacher使用已放行的LEWM检查站和数据集,而PointMaze-Medium则使用[19]的公用D4RL LeWM检查站进行安全舱载. 由于PointMaze-Large没有释放出检查站,我们用默认的脚本在OGBench指向-大navigate上对LEWM进行训练,在1个GPU上为10个3000个批次的去向提供1000个步数的1000多集. 如表A5所概述,这一数值为200克节点、199克时间边缘和2.3M相邻边缘。 对于图9中看不见的数据集图,我们使OGBench指针-大指针与完全相同的环境类,对照所储存的训练框架验证像素和编码协议,并用被冻结的模型来编码这些帧.

blocks.en: All environments share identical graph construction rules with k = 10 k{=}10 neighbours, 5-step nodes, and the empirical 1-block median threshold τ \tau . On PointMaze-Medium, building the graph takes 51 s once, and one CPU Dijkstra search takes 84 to 93 ms across three timed runs. In interleaved timed runs at d = 100 d{=}100 across 10 pairs and 3 repeats, one planning decision averages 0.8 to 1.5 s for LeWM, 2.6 s for LeWM with min-over-plan, and 1.8 s for Graph Anchors. Because solved episodes finish early, wall-clock episode time mixes solve rate and compute cost, so exact per-step GPU overhead is isolated separately in Table A17 b. For offline diagnostics, Figure 2 a and Figure A3 rebuild identical CPU graphs from stored node latents, testing 300 goals with up to 4 states per hop up to h = 40 h{=}40 and 200 pairs per distance in Figure A3 .

blocks.en: To verify that neighbour edges do not create illegal shortcuts across walls or teleports, we count how many neighbour edges span a larger physical distance than the 95th percentile of a real five-step move. These false-shortcut rates are tiny on every benchmark, measuring 0.0% on PointMaze-Medium, 0.0% on Two-Room, and 0.2% on Push-T, while more than 94% of neighbour edges bridge distinct episodes. Checking all 994,834 unique neighbour edges on PointMaze-Medium finds zero wall crossings, as reported in Table A17 b.
blocks.zh: 为了证实邻居边缘不会制造非法的捷径穿过墙壁或电传口,我们算出有多少邻居边缘跨越了比实际五步移动的第95分之多的物理距离. 这些假短率在每一个基准上都很小,在PointMaze-Medium上测量了0.0 %,在双室上测量了0.0 %,在Push-T上测量了0.2%,而超过94%的相邻边缘则会形成截然不同的情况。 如表A17b所报告,在Maze-Medium点上,检查所有994 834个独特的相邻边缘发现零墙口。

blocks.en: On Push-T, however, accurate local edges alone are not enough. When neighbour edges carry the same weight λ = 1 \lambda{=}1 as temporal edges, unweighted shortest paths jump repeatedly between different recorded episodes. Across full d = 150 d{=}150 routes in Table A17 a, 53.4% of edges are cross-episode switches rather than recorded temporal transitions, and that share rises to 64% inside the first six hops where anchors are selected, averaging 8.2 switches per 6-hop anchor over 400 paths. Jumping between demos mid-push breaks continuous block contact. Raising the neighbour edge weight to λ = 3 \lambda{=}3 , illustrated in Figure A10 c, cuts switches per anchor to 4.6, and down to 3.1 at λ = 10 \lambda{=}10 , while keeping every node reachable. This observation directly motivates the contact setting evaluated in Section C.2 .

blocks.en: Because our original PointMaze-Large LeWM checkpoint from Table 1 was no longer stored on disk, we trained a second model from scratch using the exact same code, data, and hyperparameters. As shown in Table A7 , absolute success shifts modestly between training runs. For Graph Anchors in the navigation setting, d = 400 d{=}400 success moves from 87% to 76% and stitched success moves from 66% to 45%. Importantly, the relative separation stays wide, with Graph Anchors remaining far ahead of LeWM, LeWM with min-over-plan, and every training-free alternative from Section 5.5 at every distance. The PointMaze-Large contact setting in Table 1 ran on this second checkpoint. As expected on a 400-step maze, taking small 2-move anchors exhausts the step budget before reaching the goal, scoring 13% at d = 400 d{=}400 and 9% on stitched pairs.

blocks.en: Because every seed fixes the exact same 50 start and goal pairs across methods, we can test gains cleanly on paired episodes. For each pair of methods, we pool all shared seeds and apply an exact two-sided McNemar test to the episodes where one method succeeds and the other fails. Against both LeWM and LeWM with min-over-plan, every improvement of Graph Anchors at d ≥ 50 d{\geq}50 and on stitched goals is statistically significant at p < 10 − 2 p<10^{-2} , and most reach p < 10 − 6 p<10^{-6} . The sole non-significant cell is Two-Room at d = 25 d{=}25 versus min-over-plan, where both methods are already near ceiling. Against GCBC, gains at d = 200 d{=}200 and on stitched goals are significant while d = 100 d{=}100 is not. Likewise, building the graph from random play does not differ significantly from the expert graph, and feeding held graph waypoints to GCBC makes it significantly worse at d = 200 d{=}200 .

blocks.en: When a task’s goals already lie within the reliable range of the visual cost, stopping at intermediate anchors adds unnecessary detours. Enabling our goal handoff from Figure A10 b, which scores any rollout coming within τ \tau of z g z_{g} directly by d g d_{g} and all others by d a + τ d_{a}+\tau , eliminates those detours. As shown in Figure A11 a, Reacher success rises from 66% to 86% at d = 100 d{=}100 and from 68% to 80% at d = 150 d{=}150 , outperforming min-over-plan by 12 and 2 points across five runs per setting. blocks.en: Importantly, handoff must be gated by graph distance so it cannot fire prematurely through walls. On Two-Room at d = 75 d{=}75 on seed 0, leaving handoff ungated causes the visual cost to latch onto goals behind the dividing wall and drops success to 72%. Gating handoff at 12 graph hops restores Two-Room to 87% and preserves 86% on PointMaze-Medium at d = 200 d{=}200 . Tightening the gate to 8 hops still preserves Two-Room at 92%, but lowers Reacher to 70% at d = 100 d{=}100 and 64% at d = 150 d{=}150 . Because handoff fires on nearly every step once the gate opens, we present it as an optional short-range switch rather than altering the default method.

blocks.en: We train PLDM [ 38 ] , DINO-WM [ 45 ] , GCBC, GCIVL, GCIQL [ 33 ] , and HILP [ 32 ] inside the exact same stable-worldmodel codebase on identical datasets, test pairs, and budgets. All offline policies act in closed loop from frozen DINOv2 features plus proprioceptive goal state, trained for one epoch of up to 5,000 batches of size 128 per phase. PLDM trains for one epoch of 10,000 batches and plans with LeWM’s CEM setup. DINO-WM trains for five epochs of 5,000 batches and plans directly over patch tokens. Because DINO-WM takes 37 to 68 s per decision on an H200 GPU, more than 20 × 20\times slower than LeWM, we evaluate it on 20 seed-0 pairs at long distances.

blocks.en: A natural question is whether simply adding a graph on top of an offline policy already solves long-horizon visual planning. Prior methods like GAS [ 4 ] , which builds a graph in HILP temporal-distance space ϕ \phi , and TTGS [ 30 ] , which builds a test-time graph from learned value distance log ⁡ ( V ⁡ ( 1 − γ ) + 1 ) / log ⁡ γ \log(V(1{-}\gamma){+}1)/\log\gamma , take exactly this approach. Examining both their graph construction in Table A14 and their closed-loop execution in Table A15 reveals three coupled failure modes that Graph Anchors directly resolves: 1. Metric coupling and the sharp τ \tau threshold jump. Both GAS and TTGS connect nodes by thresholding a learned value or temporal-distance head at d V < τ d_{V}<\tau , requiring per-task and per-agent τ \tau tuning. Whenever that learned head saturates on visual mazes, it outputs nearly the same high distance for almost every pair of states, leaving no usable τ \tau window at all. On simpler Two-Room, GCIVL predicts a healthy median distance of 2.9, so both TTGS and GAS form local edges and solve over 82% of goals in Table A14 . On PointMaze-Medium and PointMaze-Large, however, GCIVL distances cluster near 24 to 25. Any threshold below that plateau, such as τ ≤ 16 \tau{\leq}16 , leaves TTGS with zero value edges out of more than 142k candidates, disconnecting episodes completely. Raising τ \tau just past the plateau flips straight to 100% of all candidates , turning an empty graph directly into a dense graph full of false shortcuts that solves only 0% on PointMaze-Medium and 5% on PointMaze-Large. GAS hits a related collapse, shrinking PointMaze-Large from 2,837 nodes down to just 75 nodes at τ = 16 \tau{=}16 and admitting every edge at τ ≥ 24 \tau{\geq}24 , yet solving at most 19% on PointMaze-Medium and 2% on PointMaze-Large. Resolution. blocks.en: Figure A15 and Figure A16 show LeWM wandering near the start while Graph Anchors steer smoothly around maze walls. Inspecting every traced PointMaze-Medium failure on seed 0, covering 4 of 50 episodes at d = 200 d{=}200 and 1 of 50 stitched episodes, confirms that anchors stayed active with zero stalls. Specifically, 4 of 4 failed d = 200 d{=}200 episodes came within 0.5 maze cells of an anchor and ended 1.4 to 2.2 units from the goal. Remaining failures therefore come from slow progress along valid routes rather than wrong paths or traps.
